Secular state: 4 features of India's Constitution. Class 10 Political Science, Gender, Religion and Caste.

• The Indian state has no official religion
• Freedom to profess, practice and propagate any religion, or to follow none
• No discrimination on the grounds of religion
• The state can intervene in religious matters to ensure equality within religious communities; for example, it bans untouchability, a caste practice
• A secular constitution is necessary but not enough: communal prejudice has to be countered in everyday life and politics too
